Branchial arch.question: The _____ was Bony "loops" present in fish, which support the gills.
Branchial arch.fact: Branchial arches or gill arches are a series of paired bony/cartilaginous "loops" behind the throat (pharyngeal cavity) of fish, which support the fish gills. In all jawed fish (gnathostomes), the first arch pair (mandibular arches) develops into the jaw, the second gill arches (the hyoid arches) develop into the hyomandibular complex (which supports the back of the jaw and the front of the gill series), and the remaining posterior arches (simply called branchial arches) support the gills.

Aneurysm.fact: An aneurysm is an outward bulging, likened to a bubble or balloon, caused by a localized, abnormal, weak spot on a blood vessel wall. Aneurysms may be a result of a hereditary condition or an acquired disease.

Aneurysm.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Aneurysm.question: Unlike crystalline materials whose linear elastic region follows _____'s law under uniaxial loading, many biomaterials exhibit a J-shaped stress-strain curve which is non-linear and concave up
Aneurysm.fact: Unlike crystalline materials whose linear elastic region follows Hooke's law under uniaxial loading, many biomaterials exhibit a J-shaped stress-strain curve which is non-linear and concave up. The area under the curve up to a given strain is much lower than that for the equivalent Hookean curve, which is correlated to toughness.

Aneurysm.question: The area under the curve up to a given strain is much lower than that for the equivalent _____ curve, which is correlated to toughness
Aneurysm.fact: The area under the curve up to a given strain is much lower than that for the equivalent Hookean curve, which is correlated to toughness.

Aneurysm.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Aneurysm.fact: Endovascular coiling was introduced by Italian neurosurgeon Guido Guglielmi at University of California, Los Angeles in 1989.

Arthritis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Arthritis.question: The _____ was Type of joint disorder.
Arthritis.fact: Arthritis is a general medical term used to describe a disorder in which the smooth cartilagenous layer that lines a joint is lost, resulting in bone grinding on bone during joint movement. In certain types of arthritis, other organs, such as the skin, are also affected.

Arthritis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Arthritis.question: Osteoclast activity can be directly induced by osteoblasts through the _____/RANKL mechanism
Arthritis.fact: One of the main triggers of bone erosion in the joints in rheumatoid arthritis is inflammation of the synovium (lining of the joint capsule), caused in part by the production of pro-inflammatory cytokines and receptor activator of nuclear factor kappa B ligand (RANKL), a cell surface protein present in Th17 cells and osteoblasts. Osteoclast activity can be directly induced by osteoblasts through the RANK/RANKL mechanism.

Arthritis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Arthritis.question: In fact, about 90% of patients with _____ have musculoskeletal involvement
Arthritis.fact: In fact, about 90% of patients with Lupus have musculoskeletal involvement. Other features commonly seen in patients with Lupus include a skin rash (pictured on the right), extreme photosensitivity, hair loss, kidney problems, and shortness of breath secondary to scarring that occurs in the lungs.

Arthritis.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Arthritis.question: Within recent years, the virus _____-CoV-2, which causes COVID-19, has been added to this list
Arthritis.fact: Within recent years, the virus SARS-CoV-2, which causes COVID-19, has been added to this list. SARS-CoV-2 tends to cause reactive arthritis rather than local septic arthritis.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: The _____ was Increased pressure in a body compartment.
Compartment syndrome.fact: Compartment syndrome is a serious medical condition in which increased pressure within a body compartment compromises blood flow and tissue function, potentially leading to permanent damage if not promptly treated. Acute compartment syndrome can lead to a loss of the affected limb due to tissue death.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: German surgeon Richard von Volkmann first described compartment syndrome in _____
Compartment syndrome.fact: German surgeon Richard von Volkmann first described compartment syndrome in 1881.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: Delayed treatment can cause pain, nerve damage, cosmetic changes, and _____'s contracture
Compartment syndrome.fact: German surgeon Richard von Volkmann first described compartment syndrome in 1881. Delayed treatment can cause pain, nerve damage, cosmetic changes, and Volkmann's contracture.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: Common symptoms are: _____: A person may feel pain greater than the exam findings
Compartment syndrome.fact: In chronic exertional compartment syndrome, the pain will dissipate with rest. They are called the "5 Ps": pain, pallor, decreased pulse, paresthesia, and paralysis.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: Uncommon symptoms are: _____: Paralysis of the limb is a rare, late finding
Compartment syndrome.fact: Uncommon symptoms are: Paralysis: Paralysis of the limb is a rare, late finding.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: The pathophysiology of _____ is not entirely understood
Compartment syndrome.fact: The pathophysiology of CECS is not entirely understood. In CECS, pressure in an anatomical compartment increases due to a 20% increase in muscle volume.

Compartment syndrome.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Compartment syndrome.question: In _____, pressure in an anatomical compartment increases due to a 20% increase in muscle volume
Compartment syndrome.fact: The pathophysiology of CECS is not entirely understood. In CECS, pressure in an anatomical compartment increases due to a 20% increase in muscle volume.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Complication (medicine).fact: A complication in medicine, or medical complication, is an unfavorable result of a disease, health condition, or treatment. Complications may adversely affect the prognosis, or outcome, of a disease.

Complication (medicine).question: Surgical: _____-related medical errors can be anesthesia-related, but most often include wrong-site and wrong-patient procedural errors
Complication (medicine).fact: Surgical: Surgery-related medical errors can be anesthesia-related, but most often include wrong-site and wrong-patient procedural errors.

Complication (medicine).fact: Diagnostic: Diagnostic errors include misdiagnosis, wrong diagnosis, and over diagnosis. Diagnostic errors are often the result of patient characteristics and physician bias.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture

Complication (medicine).fact: Diagnostic errors are often the result of patient characteristics and physician bias. Machine interface: Errors in this category refer to mistakes in human interaction with tools or machines.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Complication (medicine).question: Human factors, teamwork, and communication: _____ in this category highlight the impact of culture and relationships on communication
Complication (medicine).fact: Machine interface: Errors in this category refer to mistakes in human interaction with tools or machines. Machine-related errors can be reduced by standardization and clear differentiation in design of products.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Complication (medicine).question: Common microbes involved in HAIs are _____ coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Clostridioides difficile
Complication (medicine).fact: Common microbes involved in HAIs are Escherichia coli, Proteus mirabilis, and Clostridioides difficile.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Complication (medicine).question: Diabetes mellitus may present a series of complications in an advanced or more severe stage, such as: _____ disease
Complication (medicine).fact: Diabetes mellitus may present a series of complications in an advanced or more severe stage, such as: Cardiovascular disease. Diabetes is associated with risk factors for various cardiovascular diseases including obesity, insulin resistance, high blood cholesterol and triglyceride content, and high blood pressure.

Complication (medicine).subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Complication (medicine).question: Rheumatic fever is believed to be the result of an autoimmune reaction to various tissues in the body that are similar to toxins produced by _____ pyogenes
Complication (medicine).fact: Rheumatic fever is believed to be the result of an autoimmune reaction to various tissues in the body that are similar to toxins produced by Streptococcus pyogenes.

Contracture.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Contracture.question: The _____ was Permanent shortening of a muscle or joint.
Contracture.fact: In pathology, a contracture is a shortening of muscles, tendons, skin, and nearby soft tissues that causes the joints to shorten and become very stiff, preventing normal movement. A contracture is usually permanent, but less commonly can be temporary (such as in McArdle disease), or resolve over time but reoccur later in life (such as in Bethlem myopathy 1).

Contracture.fact: Immobilization, A muscle imbalance between an agonist and antagonist muscle, In response to impending muscle damage associated with ATP (energy) deficiency, Congenital abnormalities of muscle development.

Corticosteroid.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Corticosteroid.question: The _____ was Class of steroid hormones.
Corticosteroid.fact: Corticosteroids are a class of steroid hormones that are produced in the adrenal cortex of vertebrates, and also their synthetic analogues. The two main classes of corticosteroids – glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids – are involved in a wide range of physiological processes, including stress response, immune response, and regulation of inflammation, carbohydrate metabolism, protein catabolism, blood electrolyte levels, and behavior.

Corticosteroid.fact: In 1952, D.H. Peterson and H.C. Murray of Upjohn developed a process that used Rhizopus mold to oxidize progesterone into a compound that was readily converted to cortisone.

Corticosteroid.subject: Fisheries & Aquaculture
Corticosteroid.question: The ability to cheaply synthesize large quantities of cortisone from the diosgenin in yams resulted in a rapid drop in price to US$6 per gram, falling to $0.46 per gram by _____
